# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_003_page_001.jpg

---

3:1 The souls of the righteous are held safe in the hand of God. No suffering can reach them there.

3:2 To the foolish, they appeared to have died. Their passing looked like disaster,

3:3 their departure from us like complete annihilation. But they are at peace.

3:4 Yes — though the world saw them punished, they were carrying a hope charged with immortality.

3:5 A little discipline, and then great blessing. God tested them and found them worthy of himself.

3:6 He refined them like gold in a furnace. He received them like a sacrifice offered whole to him.

3:7 When the time comes for God to act, they will blaze out in glory — darting like sparks through a dry field of stubble.

3:8 They will render judgment over nations. They will govern peoples. And the Lord will reign over them forever.

3:9 Those who trust in him will come to know the truth. The faithful will live with him in love. His holy ones receive grace and mercy. His chosen ones are under his care.

3:10 The ungodly will face a punishment that matches their thinking — those who turned their backs on righteousness and walked away from the Lord.

3:11 Whoever despises wisdom and the discipline that comes with it has nothing. Their hope is hollow. Their hard work amounts to nothing. Their deeds have no lasting value.

3:12 Their wives are foolish; their children have gone bad. The whole line is under a curse.

3:13 But blessed is the barren woman who remained pure — who never knew a bed stained by wrongdoing. At the time when souls are called to account, she will receive her fruit.

3:14 And blessed is the man who was unable to father children but never used that powerlessness to do wrong, never let bitterness turn him against the Lord. He will be given a rare and special gift — a most welcome place in the temple of the Lord.

3:15 The fruit of honest work is radiant. Understanding never runs dry at its root.

3:16 The children of adulterers will never come to full maturity. The offspring of unlawful unions will vanish away.

3:17 They may live long lives, but they will be counted as nothing. Whatever age they reach, they will die without honor.

3:18 And if they die young, they will face the day of judgment with neither hope nor anyone to speak for them.

3:19 The end of a wicked generation is pitiless.

---

*PNEUMA notes: 3:1 is rendered with deliberate weight — the verse demands to be heard. "Held safe in the hand of God" rather than simply "are in the hand" makes the security concrete. Verse 7's "blaze out in glory" captures the eschatological fire-imagery. Verse 14 expands slightly to convey the eunuch's existential situation — the author is invoking Isaiah 56:3-5 and deserves a rendering that makes the compassion legible. Verse 19 uses "pitiless" for ponēra — capturing the merciless finality.*
